newsitem.title: MEXICO: Hylsamex signs $100 mln export-backed credit.
newsitem.headline: Hylsamex signs $100 mln export-backed credit.

text.p: Mexican steel company Hylsamex said on Wednesday it signed a $100 million export-backed credit with a group of banks.
The financing was lead by Santander Investment, and was boosted from an originally planned $80 million, a Hylsamex director who declined to be named told Reuters.
The six-year credit will have a rate of 150 points over LIBOR, he said.

The director said the credit will be used for the company's expansion program through 1998, with the main investment being a mini-mill oven construction for flat steel. The project is expected to double production capacity to 1.5 million tonnes.
Hylsamex already receives funding from Eximbanks from the United States, Canada, Germany and Italy for a total of more than $100 million in 1997 and 1998.
The company is a subsidiary of conglomerate Alfa, and had sales of more than $1.15 billion in 1996 and produced 2.4 million tonnes. ((-- Daniel Prez-Whitaker, Monterrey bureau +528 345 7617))
